title: Read compiler output
description:
Write a C function in assembly the way a compiler would, then compare.

```
sum_to(10) = 55
sum_to(0) = 0
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .text
sum_to:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

_start:
        mov     edi, 10
        call    sum_to
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: At `-O2`, GCC often replaces the loop with the formula n × (n + 1) / 2, or uses `lea` for the additions (lesson 6.01).
`test rdi, rdi` / `jle .done` handles 0 and negative numbers before the loop.
requirements: The C version is `long sum_to(long n) { long s = 0; for (long i = 1; i <= n; i++) s += i; return s; }`.
Write it by hand, then look at what GCC produces with `-O2` on Compiler Explorer and write down one difference in a comment.
stretch: Compile with `-O0` too and explain why it is so much longer.
